reasoning: For every horizontal scanline inside the vertical span of a connected simple orthogonal polygon, exactly its leftmost and rightmost boundary intersections are visible from the two horizontal directions. Integrating gives visible vertical-wall length twice the height span, regardless of concavities. The vertical-scanline analogue gives twice the width span. Subtract these exposed lengths from the Manhattan perimeter; vertex-level ties have zero length and do not affect the measure.
